t.2.96.1: Vasiṣṭha, placing the wives of Daśaratha before him, approached that place, thirsting for the sight of Rāma.
t.2.96.2: And the royal wives, going slowly toward the Mandākinī, saw there that bathing place frequented by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.96.3: Kausalyā, her face filled with tears and withering with grief, spoke to Sumitrā and to the other royal ladies, who were all downcast.
t.2.96.5: From here, O Sumitrā, your son Saumitri, ever untiring, himself fetches water for the sake of my son.
t.2.96.4: This is the hardship of those helpless ones whose deeds were never harsh: here in the forest, formerly a mere bathing place, dwell those who have been banished from the realm.
t.2.96.6: On the ground, upon darbha grass with its tips pointing south, the long-eyed lady saw the cake of iṅguda pulp that had been offered for her father-in-law.
t.2.96.7: Seeing it laid on the ground for his father by the grief-stricken Rāma, Queen Kausalyā spoke to all the wives of Daśaratha.
t.2.96.8: Behold this, given according to rule by Rāghava to his father, the great-souled Rāghava, lord of the Ikṣvākus.
t.2.96.9: I do not think this food is fitting for that great-souled king, the equal of the gods, who had enjoyed every pleasure.
t.2.96.10: That mighty lord of the earth, equal to great Indra, who enjoyed the earth bounded on four sides, how is it that he now eats a cake of pressed iṅguda seeds?
t.2.96.11: Nothing in the world seems to me more sorrowful than this, that Rāma, though endowed with prosperity, should offer his father a paste of pounded iṅgudī fruit.
t.2.96.12: Seeing the iṅguda oil-cake offered by Rāma to his father, how is it that my heart does not burst into a thousand pieces from grief?
t.2.96.13: Then her co-wives, having comforted her who was thus distressed, went on, and in the hermitage they saw Rāma, like an immortal fallen from heaven.
t.2.96.14: Seeing Rāma bereft of all comforts, the mothers, distressed and worn down by grief, shed tears and wept aloud.
t.2.96.15: Rising up, Rāma, tiger among men, true to his promise, clasped the auspicious feet of all those mothers.
t.2.96.16: Those long-eyed women, with their lovely hands, pleasant to the touch, with soft fingers and palms, wiped the dust from Rāma's back.
t.2.96.17: Saumitri too, grieved at beholding all those mothers, slowly and devotedly saluted them right after Rāma.
t.2.96.18: All the women conducted themselves toward Lakṣmaṇa, born of Daśaratha and marked with auspicious signs, just as they did toward Rāma.
t.2.96.19: Sītā too, grief-stricken, clasped the feet of her mothers-in-law, and she stood before them, her eyes brimming with tears.
t.2.96.20: Embracing her, afflicted with sorrow, wretched and emaciated from dwelling in the forest, as a mother embraces her daughter, Kausalyā spoke these words.
t.2.96.21: How has the daughter of the king of Videha, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha and the wife of Rāma, come to suffer such sorrow in this desolate forest?
t.2.96.23: O Vaidehī, as I look upon your face, grief born from the fire-sticks of misfortune burns me fiercely within my mind, as fire consumes the thing it rests upon.
t.2.96.22: He was like a lotus scorched by the heat of the sun, like a withered water lily, like gold tarnished by dust, like the moon dimmed by clouds.
t.2.96.24: While his distressed mother was speaking thus, Rāghava, the elder brother of Bharata, approached Vasiṣṭha and clasped his feet.
t.2.96.25: Just as Indra, lord of the immortals, clasps the feet of Bṛhaspati, so Rāghava clasped the feet of that family priest, who was like fire and of abundant splendour, and sat down together with him.
t.2.96.27: Then the valiant Bharata, having beheld Rāghava blazing with splendour in the garb of an ascetic, sat down near him with joined palms, devout and self-restrained, as great Indra sits before Prajāpati.
t.2.96.26: Then righteous Bharata, together with the ministers, the chief men of the city and the soldiers, and with people most versed in dharma, sat down humbly in a lower place beside his elder brother.
t.2.96.28: “What fitting words will this Bharata speak today to Rāghava, after bowing to him and paying him honour?” In just this way, a supreme curiosity truly arose then in that assembly of noble people.
t.2.96.29: That Rāghava, steadfast in truth, and the noble-minded Lakṣmaṇa, and the righteous Bharata, surrounded by their friends, shone like the three sacred fires at a sacrifice, accompanied by the officiating priests.
